title: Action — normalize Vaporize package and executable identity conventions
description: Adopt the existing Tool Interface and Language Naming Standard for Vaporize. The SwiftPM package coordinate is vaporize@wrkstrm-core.cli, matching the package home. The new canonical executable product is vaporize.cli-s@wrkstrm-core.clia.sh because Vaporize is implemented by a SwiftPM executable target. The former bare cli product is historical compatibility only, not a second active canonical identity. Typed identity documentation distinguishes package coordinate, executable product, installed binary, metadata sidecar, interface, implementation language, owner, and human display name.
acceptanceCriteria: Package.swift declares vaporize@wrkstrm-core.cli as the package name.
Package.swift declares vaporize.cli-s@wrkstrm-core.clia.sh as the single active executable product.
The command parser, docs, source-generated receipts, and current identity record use the Tool Interface and Language Naming Standard rather than restating a local grammar.
The former vaporize.cli@wrkstrm-core.clia.sh spelling is retained only where source compatibility or historical evidence requires it; it is never presented as a second canonical identity.

The refreshed installed metadata sidecar names the language-qualified canonical executable, CLI interface, Swift language code, unique version, and unique build after installed-runtime parity is repaired in its separate bug Bead.
Focused source build and installed --version checks are recorded separately under the language-qualified canonical executable name.
risks: Changing the executable name without a declared migration leaves exact routes and installed artifacts split; the source migration and installed-runtime cutover must be independently receipted.
Treating the former bare cli spelling as a language claim would rewrite historical provenance; it remains a language-null compatibility record.
Reinstalling without unique version/build metadata would leave two materially different source states indistinguishable in fleet evidence.
